text: One night, young Yusuf had a wonderful dream. He saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon, all bowing down to him.
Tap every star, the sun and the moon, and watch them bow.
Yusuf told his father, Yaqub. His father said: my son, do not tell your brothers about this dream. Allah will choose you, and teach you the meaning of dreams.
What did his father Yaqub tell Yusuf to do about the dream?
Tell all his brothers
Keep it from his brothers
Not quite. His father said: do not tell your brothers.

Yusuf's brothers were jealous. They said: our father loves Yusuf more than us! So they made a bad plan. Some of them wanted to get rid of him. But one said: do not hurt him. Leave him in a deep well, where travellers may find him.
They took Yusuf far away and put him down into a deep, dark well.
But down in the dark, Yusuf was not alone. Allah comforted his heart: one day, you will tell your brothers about all this, and they will not even know it is you.
That night the brothers came home crying. They said: Father, a wolf ate Yusuf! And they showed him Yusuf's shirt, stained to make their story look true.
Look closely at the shirt, just as Yaqub did. A wolf has sharp teeth. Is the shirt torn?
Yes, it is torn
No, not one tear
Look again. The shirt is stained, but there is not one tear in it.
A wolf would have torn the shirt to pieces. So what do you think? Was the brothers' story true?
Yes, a wolf did it
No, it was not true
Not quite. The wolf did nothing at all! Try again.
No, it was not true, and their father Yaqub knew it. He said: it is best to be patient. I ask Allah alone for help.
The brothers were jealous of Yusuf.
They put Yusuf down into the well.
They showed their father the shirt.
Yaqub chose to be patient.
Some travellers came by. They sent a man to fetch water, and he let his bucket down into the well.
Help him pull! Drag the rope up, or tap fast, to bring the bucket up.
Good news! shouted the man. Here is a boy! The travellers hid Yusuf away to sell him. But Allah knew everything they did.
What did the man shout when he saw Yusuf?
Good news! Here is a boy!
Oh no, my bucket!
Listen again. He shouted: good news!
Yusuf was sold for a very small price: just a few silver coins. Tap the coins to count them.
Twenty small coins. They did not know how precious Yusuf was.
So Yusuf was carried far from home, all the way to the land of Egypt.
Drag the camel along the path, or tap it, to help the caravan cross the desert.
In Egypt, a man bought Yusuf and took him to his home. He told his wife: look after him well.
What did the man say to his wife about Yusuf?
Send him away
Look after him well
No. He said: look after him well.
The years passed, and Yusuf grew into a young man in Egypt. When he was grown, Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge.
One day, the woman of the house tried to make Yusuf do something wrong. Yusuf said: Allah forbid! My master has been good to me. And he ran for the door.
She pulled at his shirt from behind, and it tore. At the door they met her husband. She said that Yusuf was to blame. But Yusuf said: she is the one who tried to make me do wrong.
A wise person in the house said: look at his shirt. If it is torn at the front, she is telling the truth. If it is torn at the back, Yusuf is.
Where is Yusuf's shirt torn?
At the front
At the back
Not that way. Remember, she pulled it from behind.
The shirt was torn at the back! So everyone could see that Yusuf was telling the truth.
But people kept on talking, and the woman kept on at him. Yusuf prayed: My Lord, prison is better for me than what they ask of me. And Allah answered his prayer and kept him safe from doing wrong.
Everyone had seen the signs that Yusuf was innocent. But in the end they put him in prison for a while anyway.
Be patient, like Yusuf. Press and hold the lamp until it shines. Don't let go!
Yusuf stayed patient in prison, and he never stopped trusting Allah.
Yusuf ran for the door.
His shirt was torn from behind.
A wise person said: look at the shirt.
Yusuf was put in prison, and he stayed patient.
Two young men were in prison with Yusuf. Each of them had a dream, and they asked Yusuf what the dreams meant.
First, Yusuf told them the most important thing: worship no one but Allah, the One.
What was the first thing Yusuf told the two men?
Worship Allah alone
Dig a tunnel
No. First he told them: worship no one but Allah.
Now match each dream to its meaning. Tap a dream, then tap what it means.
I dreamed I was pressing grapes.
I dreamed birds ate the bread I carried on my head.
You will be saved, and you will serve your master.
A sad end. You will be put to death.
Yusuf said to the man who would go free: tell your master about me. But the man forgot. So Yusuf stayed in prison for more years.
Then the king had a strange dream. Seven fat cows were eaten by seven thin cows. And he saw seven green ears of grain, and seven dry ones.
Seven fat cows! Can you find them? Tap all seven of the fat cows.
Nobody could explain it. Then the man from the prison remembered Yusuf at last! He hurried to ask him.
Tap each side of the dream to hear what Yusuf said it means.
The fat cows and the green grain: seven good years are coming. Plant, and save what you harvest.
The thin cows and the dry grain: then seven hard years will come, and you will eat what you saved.
And after that, said Yusuf, will come a year with plenty of rain.
Help the people get ready. Is each job for the good years, or for the hard years?
Good years
Hard years
Plant the fields
Eat what was saved
Save the grain
Open the storehouse
Bring in the harvest
Think again. Save in the good years, and use it in the hard years.
The king said: bring Yusuf to me! But Yusuf did not hurry out of prison. He said: first, find out what really happened to me.

So the king asked the women who had spoken against Yusuf: what really happened? They said: Allah forbid! We know nothing bad about him. And the woman of the house said: Now the truth is out. It was I who tried to make him do wrong. Yusuf is an honest man.
Put the story in order. Tap what happened first, then what came next.
Yusuf asked for the truth to be found.
The king asked what had happened.
The woman told the truth.
The king trusted Yusuf.
Not yet. Think about what came first.
The king trusted Yusuf completely. Yusuf said: put me in charge of the storehouses. I will look after them with care.
The good years are here! Tap the grain as it grows, and save it in the storehouse.
The storehouse is full. The grain is saved, just as Yusuf said.
Later, Yusuf's brothers travelled to Egypt to get grain for their family.
Yusuf knew them at once. But they did not know it was him!
Did the brothers know who he was?
Yes, straight away
No, they did not know him
No. Yusuf knew them, but they did not know him.
Yusuf gave them full measure. Tap each sack until it is full to the top.
Yusuf said: next time, bring your other brother, the one at home with your father. And he had their payment put back in their bags.
Help put their payment back. Tap each sack to tuck the payment inside.
Before the brothers set off again, their father Yaqub said: my sons, do not all go in by one gate. Go in by different gates. I trust in Allah.
Do as their father said. Tap a gate for each brother, a different gate each time.
The brothers came again, and this time they brought their brother. Yusuf took him aside and said: I am your brother. Do not be sad.
Then came a plan that Allah made for Yusuf, so that his brother could stay with him. The king's drinking cup was placed in his brother's bag.
Whose plan was this, so that his brother could stay?
Allah made it for Yusuf
The brothers made it
No. This was a plan that Allah made for Yusuf.
The king's cup is missing! Search the bags one by one, starting with the oldest brother's.
Not in this one.
There it is, in his brother's bag! So his brother stayed in Egypt with Yusuf.
Back at home, their father Yaqub was full of sorrow. He missed Yusuf so much that his eyes turned white with grief.
But Yaqub did not lose hope. He said: my sons, go and look for Yusuf and his brother. Never lose hope in Allah's mercy.

So the brothers went back to Egypt. Then he asked them: do you know what you did to Yusuf? They cried: could it be that you are Yusuf? He said: I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Allah has been good to us.
The brothers hung their heads. They said: By Allah, Allah chose you over us, and we were in the wrong.
The brothers said they were sorry. What did Yusuf do?
He sent them away
He forgave them
No. Yusuf did something much more beautiful. Try again.
Yusuf forgave them! He said: you will hear no blame today. May Allah forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of all.
Yaqub said: never lose hope.
Yusuf said: I am Yusuf.
The brothers said: we were in the wrong.
Yusuf forgave them.
Yusuf gave them his shirt. He said: lay it over my father's face, and he will see again. Then bring your whole family to me.
Far away, as the caravan set off, a wind began to blow. And Yaqub said: I can smell Yusuf!
Drag the shirt along the path, or tap it, to carry the good news home.
The shirt was laid on Yaqub's face, and he could see again! The brothers said: Father, ask Allah to forgive us. And he said: I will ask my Lord to forgive you.
What happened when the shirt was laid on Yaqub's face?
He fell asleep
He could see again
No. Something wonderful happened: he could see again!
The whole family came to Egypt. Yusuf held his parents close and said: welcome to Egypt. You will all be safe here, if Allah wills.
Tap the stars, the sun and the moon, just like in the dream.
They all bowed down before him. Yusuf said: Father, this is what my dream meant, long ago. My Lord has made it come true.
Look back at the dream. Who were the eleven stars?
His eleven brothers
Eleven camels
Think again. Who came to Egypt to bow before Yusuf?
Yes! The eleven stars were his eleven brothers, and the sun and the moon were his father and mother. The dream had come true.
What have we learned from Yusuf? For each one, tap: like Yusuf, or not like Yusuf.
Like Yusuf
Not like Yusuf
Being patient
Making up a story
Telling the truth
Staying angry
Forgiving
Trusting Allah
Think about what Yusuf did.
Then Yusuf prayed: My Lord, You are my protector in this world and the next. Let me die devoted to You, and join me with the righteous.
This picture is all mixed up! Tap two pieces to swap them, until the picture is whole again.
Find the pairs. Tap two cards. If they match, they stay.
The end. Yusuf was patient, he told the truth, and he forgave. What will you remember from his story?
